subjects.name: ELECTRICAL PUMPS AND VALVES OPERATION SKILL
subjects.objective: To understand the basic operating technique and working of Industrial pumps, valves, Flow measurement, and Temperature Pressure measurement device used in chemical process industries, also understand application of measuring instruments of electrical parameters, construction & operation of electrical motors used for pump and valve operation. Also understand electrical control strategy for value control as well as various electrical transducers used for flow, pressure and temperature measurement
course_outcomes: Different type of Industrial Pumps and Valves.
Different type of electrical motor used for pump and valve operation
Different Types of Flow Measurement Devices and electrical transducer used for it.
Different Types of Temperature measurement Devices and electrical transducer used for it.
Different Types of Pressure measurement Devices and electrical transducer used for it

allSyllabusUnits.title: Pumps
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of pumps and basic technology related to operation, operating practice of reciprocating pumps, Positive displacement pump, centrifugal pump, rotary pumps, Measurement of various electrical quantities and application of various electrical measuring instruments. Construction and operation of electrical motor used for all above pump application.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Valves
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of valves and basic technology related to operation and working, of Isolation valve, regulating valve, back flow prevention valve, pressure relief valve, gate valve, globe valve, ball valve and diapharm valve Working, construction and operation of electrical motor and control system used for various valve.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Flow measurement
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Classification of flow measurement devices, basic technology related to measurement. Operating practice of venturi meter, orifice meter, rotameter, pitot-tube Working, construction and operation of electrical transducer used for flow measurement devices

allSyllabusUnits.title: Temperature measurement devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Working and operating practice of Thermometer, Thermocouple, Thermistors, Thermowell and Pyrometer. Working, construction and operation of electrical transducer used for temperature measurement devices

allSyllabusUnits.title: Pressure measurement devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Working and operating practice of U-tube manometer, Inclined tube Manometer, Pressure gauge. Working, construction and operation of electrical transducer used for pressure measurement devices Total Hours 56

subjects.name: GENERATIVE AI & PROMPT ENGINEERING
subjects.objective: To enable students to understand Generative AI concepts and effectively use prompt engineering techniques to perform engineering tasks such as report generation, inspection, maintenance planning, and documentation without requiring programming knowledge.
course_outcomes: Apply the basic working principles of Generative AI to identify suitable engineering applications.
Use appropriate AI tools to perform specific engineering tasks effectively.
Construct structured and optimized prompts for solving engineering problems.
Examine and refine AI-generated outputs to improve correctness and usefulness.
Develop prompt-based solutions to handle real-world engineering workflows.

allSyllabusUnits.title: AI IN ENGINEERING PRACTICE
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Basics of Generative AI, AI working principle (prediction concept), AI vs Traditional tools, AI tools overview, Engineering applications of AI

allSyllabusUnits.title: SMART USE OF AI TOOLS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Communication with AI, AI tool capabilities & limitations, Tool selection for tasks, Common usage mistakes, Data privacy & confidentiality, Safety considerations, Bias and incorrect outputs

allSyllabusUnits.title: PROMPT DESIGN FUNDAMENTALS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to prompts and Prompt structure (task, context, format), Types of prompts, Step-by-step prompting, Problem decomposition, Example-based prompting, Prompt templates (report, checklist, SOP)

allSyllabusUnits.title: PRACTICAL ENGINEERING APPLICATIONS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Inspection applications, Maintenance applications, Safety applications, Work planning, Structured output generation, Prompt refinement, Output comparison, Workflow prompting

allSyllabusUnits.title: AI-ASSISTED EVALUATION AND ETHICS
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Using AI Tools for Code Generation, Code Debugging and Optimization, Prompt Chaining for Step-by-step Development, Detecting Hallucinations in AI-generated Code, Responsible AI Usage, Data Privacy and Security Considerations, Mini Project using Python and Prompt Engineering Total Hours 0

subjects.name: UNIT OPERATION-I
subjects.objective: To study about Mechanical Operations generally carried out in Chemical Processes Industries involving solid-solid and solid-liquid handling, mixing and separation. To study about Mechanical Operations generally carried out in ChemicalProcesses Industries involving solid-solid and solid-liquid handling, mixing and separation.
course_outcomes: Understand different properties of particulate solids and methods of out its analysis.
Express criteria for selection of specific size reduction equipments based on their application.
Be able to utilize theoretical knowledge for fundamental design of suitable solid liquid separation operation
To build a bridge between theoretical and practical concepts of unit operation used in chemical industry to solve environmental pollution problems.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Particulate Solids
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Particle characterization, Concept of sphericity, Mixed particles size, specific surface area and specific number of particles Basic terms in screening, Screen analysis- differential and cumulative analysis.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Size Reduction and Screening
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Crushing Law, Classification of size reduction equipments, Crushers, Grinders, Ultra-fine grinders, Cutting machines, Open circuit and closed circuit operation, Screen effectiveness, Ideal screen and actual screen, Different screening equipments

allSyllabusUnits.title: Filtration, Sedimentation and Centrifugal Separation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition and Mechanisms of filtration, Filtration theory, Filter media and filter aids, Classification & Selection of filtration equipments, Bag filter in air pollution control, Plate and frame filter press, Rotary drum filter etc. Batch sedimentation test, Applications of sedimentation, Theory of centrifugal separation, centrifugal filtration, Classification of centrifuges, Simple bowl centrifuge, Disc centrifuge, Tubular-bowl centrifuge, Gas centrifuge

allSyllabusUnits.title: Solid-Solid and Solid-Fluid Separation
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Magnetic Separation, Froth Floatation, Cyclone Separation and Electrostatic Precipitation Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First half of ordered syllabus units: Particulate Solids; Size Reduction and Screening; Filtration, Sedimentation and Centrifugal Separation.

Questions: [8 marks] Explain Engineering curves and their practical classification. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Constructing an ellipse by standard geometric methods. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Parabola and hyperbola construction and the focus/directrix idea. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Cycloidal curves, involutes and spirals. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
Engineering curves include conics and other geometric curves used to represent shapes or motion. Ellipses, parabolas and hyperbolas are conic sections; cycloids, epicycloids, hypocycloids, involutes and spirals are other common constructions in engineering graphics. The method is chosen according to the defining geometry and the intended use. A drawing should show construction lines clearly, use suitable instruments and identify the required tangent or normal when requested. Accuracy depends on the construction procedure and neat, unambiguous line work.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
An ellipse can be constructed by methods such as concentric circles, rectangle or oblong methods, and arc-of-circle approaches taught in the syllabus. First mark the major and minor axes and their centres accurately. Divide the relevant circles, sides or arcs into corresponding parts, project matching points and draw a smooth continuous curve through them. Select the method according to the data and construction requested. Check symmetry about both axes and use light construction lines before darkening the final curve.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A conic is defined by a geometric relation between a point and a focus/directrix or by another specified construction condition. A parabola has eccentricity one; an ellipse has eccentricity below one and a hyperbola above one. Construction methods use the given dimensions or geometric properties to locate successive points, then join them smoothly. Tangents and normals are drawn according to the prescribed method at the required point. Verify the defining dimensions and symmetry and distinguish the conics by their geometry rather than by appearance alone.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
A cycloid is traced by a point on a circle rolling along a straight line. An epicycloid is generated when a circle rolls outside another circle, while a hypocycloid is generated when it rolls inside. An involute can be understood as the path traced by the end of a taut string unwound from a base curve; spirals move progressively inward or outward according to their construction. Start from the generating geometry, divide the motion into corresponding steps, plot points carefully and construct any requested tangent or normal.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Orthographic projection represents a 3D point by projections on principal reference planes, commonly the horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP). A point's position relative to HP and VP determines its quadrant and the location of its front and top views. Use the reference line consistently, draw projectors perpendicular to it and apply the convention for distances from each plane. Label views clearly and preserve the given dimensions. Questions: [8 marks] Explain Drawing instruments, BIS conventions, line types and layout. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Representative fraction and selection of drawing scales. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Dimensioning and annotation of engineering drawings. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
[8 marks] Explain Orthographic projection and first-angle versus third-angle methods. Describe its meaning or purpose, principal features or steps, and one relevant example.
Answers:
Model answer:
A drawing sheet should have a suitable size, border, title block and layout, with space allocated for views and notes. Instruments such as drawing boards, T-squares or parallel rules, set squares, compass, divider and scale support accurate construction. Standard line conventions distinguish visible outlines, hidden edges, centre lines, dimensions and construction work. Use lettering and dimensioning consistently and choose a suitable scale when the object will not fit at full size. Standards make drawings legible and interpretable by others, rather than relying on informal assumptions.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Representative fraction (RF) is drawing length divided by actual length after both are expressed in the same units. A full-size scale has RF 1:1; a reducing scale has RF below one, and an enlarging scale has RF greater than one. For example, RF 1:5 means a 50 mm actual length is shown as 10 mm on the drawing. Select a scale that preserves legibility and available sheet space, state it clearly, and apply it consistently to dimensions and construction. The written dimension normally states actual size, not the measured paper length.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Dimensioning communicates the size and position of features. Use clear extension and dimension lines, legible figures and appropriate symbols, and avoid repeating dimensions or creating ambiguity. Choose line types according to their purpose: visible outlines, hidden details, centre lines and dimension lines should be distinguishable. Annotations should be placed near the relevant feature without clutter. A drawing should contain enough dimensions to manufacture or inspect the part, but not contradictory or redundant values. Apply the relevant standard conventions and check units and overall dimensions.

8-mark marking guide: 2 marks for the core concept; 3 marks for accurate principles, steps or formulas; 2 marks for an example/application; 1 mark for a justified conclusion or check. A strong answer should define the concept and organize the main points clearly.

Model answer:
Orthographic projection represents an object through views perpendicular to principal planes. The front view communicates height and width, the top view width and depth, and a side view height and depth. In first-angle projection, the object is between the observer and projection plane; in third-angle projection, the projection plane is between observer and object. Therefore the arrangement of views differs. Identify the projection method by its symbol or stated convention, align corresponding dimensions across views, and check that the set of views describes one consistent object.

Model answer:
A sectional view imagines the object cut by a defined plane and removes the nearer part to reveal internal geometry. The cutting plane and viewing direction must be clear; hatching indicates surfaces intersected by the cutting plane and should be spaced consistently. A section can reduce the number of hidden lines and make holes, cavities or internal profiles easier to interpret. Do not hatch empty spaces, and follow the applicable convention for adjacent parts. Compare the section with other views to ensure that the revealed internal form is geometrically consistent.

Model answer:
An isometric drawing shows three principal axes equally inclined in the representation, commonly 120 degrees apart. Isometric projection uses foreshortened lengths along the axes and therefore an isometric scale; an isometric view/drawing often uses true lengths along isometric axes as prescribed in the course. To construct an object, establish the axes, transfer width, depth and height from the orthographic views, add faces and circular features with suitable isometric constructions, then remove unnecessary construction lines. Check that all dimensions correspond to the original orthographic views.
